🇬🇧 On Monday, in Cardiff, the leaders of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland signed a document asserting their right to "self-determination" — and it barely dented the news.

John Swinney (SNP), Rhun ap Iorwerth (Plaid Cymru) and Michelle O'Neill (Sinn Féin) put their names to a memorandum covering the economy, energy, Europe and independence. They told the Government to prepare for constitutional change.

It's the first time in the history of devolution that all three nations have been led by pro-independence governments at the same time.

Let's be honest: a memorandum is not a referendum, and Westminster still has the final say. Nobody's passport changed on Monday.

But here's the problem — the man sent out to defend the Union is a Prime Minister not one voter was asked to approve. 👇
